messages.subject: optimizing the ODE integrator
parts:
Hi!

The ODE integrator currently has to deal with the ODE itself and it's sensitivities. Now, the sensitivities depend on the particular parametrization of the ODE, right? If so, then the way the user chooses the parametrization has a big impact on the performance of Stan, i.e. if a bad parametrization leads to stiff sensititivies, then this a bad thing!

Am I right here and if yes, then what techniques can you recommend to optimize?

Thanks!

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] optimizing the ODE integrator
parts: > The ODE integrator currently has to deal with the ODE itself and it's sensitivities. Now, the sensitivities depend on the particular parametrization of the ODE, right? If so, then the way the user chooses the parametrization has a big impact on the performance of Stan, i.e. if a bad parametrization leads to stiff sensititivies, then this a bad thing!

Yup, this is fundamental to how ODEs are defined (at least unless you define them
purely geometrically).
> Am I right here and if yes, then what techniques can you recommend to optimize?

There is no general procedure here. Of course it would be great if our ODEs
were all linear, but they don’t be in any practical model and the best we can hope
for is that they are not _too_ nonlinear where we evaluate them. In Bayesian
inference this is even more complicated because we don’t get to choose where
we evaluate the ODEs, the data and model assumptions define that.

In particular, we haven’t been running ODE models in Stan long enough to even
identify that many pathological models, let alone classify them by the interaction
between the parameterization and the nonlinearity of the ODEs in an attempt
to identify efficient parameterization strategies.
